gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker Prime 160W (A2687) reaches 150W only with the Anker A110A power bank on Anker cables A88E2, A82E2 or A84N1, or the A110A's own cable, and that AI Mode, which also runs its dynamic split, cannot charge DJI charging hubs.
standout_why: I compared against these cited pages: itechguides (it says the 150W-qualifying models are not named, and it covers no DJI, Samsung or Apple-cable limits), the Anker US product page (it names only 'Anker Prime Power Bank (26K, 300W)' for 150W and says nothing about DJI hubs, Apple Thunderbolt cables or phone-brand caps), the service.anker.com spec page (it shows FAQ titles without the answers), Notebookcheck news and review (they cover only UGREEN ports and display), and our own Dealectric page (it has the MacBook cable point but no 150W list, no DJI exclusion and no Samsung, Huawei, Xiaomi, vivo or OPPO caps). The Anker product page partly covers the 150W point, so the new material is Anker's support-FAQ list of exact models and exclusions.
decides: It confirms rather than reverses the pick. The Anker's two extras over the UGREEN, 150W and AI-Mode dynamic split, only work with one specific Anker power bank and specific Anker cables, and AI Mode has to be switched off for DJI drone charging hubs. So for a shopper without that Anker power bank, the $60 premium buys size and weight, not extra wattage. That strengthens 'UGREEN for value, Anker only for travel size'. Anyone who charges DJI batteries through a hub should also be told that the Anker needs USB-C1 Priority Mode or Custom Mode for it.

findings.label: Requirements for 150W from one port
findings.value: AI Mode, plus Anker power bank A110A, with Anker USB-C cables A88E2 or A82E2, Anker Thunderbolt 5 cable A84N1, or the cable included with the A110A
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, GaNPrime) FAQ
findings.note: FAQ Q6: 'To reach 150W max charging from one port, the charger must be set to AI Mode and used with the following devices and cables… Anker may release new products in the future that support 150W charging.' The US product page footnote 2 names the 'Anker Prime Power Bank (26K, 300W)' and says 'This cable is not included with the charger.'

findings.label: DJI charging hub exclusion
findings.value: DJI charging hubs do not charge in AI Mode; use USB-C1 Port Priority Mode or Custom Mode
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, GaNPrime) FAQ
findings.note: FAQ Q12: 'DJI charging hubs do not support automatic input adjustment. As a result, they cannot charge when the charger is in AI Mode.' The US product page says dynamic power distribution is 'only available in AI Mode 2.0'.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro cable for 140W
findings.value: M1 and M2: USB-C to MagSafe 3 only. M3 and M4: EPR (140W/240W) USB-C to USB-C cable or USB-C to MagSafe 3
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, GaNPrime) FAQ
findings.note: FAQ Q5. This is a MacBook-side limit, so it applies to the UGREEN's 140W ports as well. Our current page already states it, citing MacRumors.

findings.label: Apple Thunderbolt cable cap
findings.value: 60 W (Apple Thunderbolt cables of 1.8 m, 2 m and 3 m show as '3A Cable')
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, GaNPrime) FAQ
findings.note: FAQ Q15: 'Apple Thunderbolt cables (1.8 m / 2 m / 3 m) support only up to 60W and will display as 3A cables on the charger.' Also: 3A cable up to 60W, 5A up to 100W, EPR up to 240W.

findings.label: Samsung 45W Super Fast Charging 2.0
findings.value: Needs a 5A cable in AI Mode. In other modes the port must give more than 45 W. An Apple Thunderbolt cable can trip protection (water-drop warning, charging stops)
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, GaNPrime) FAQ

findings.label: Proprietary-protocol phone caps
findings.value: Huawei up to 22.5 W, Xiaomi up to 27 W, some vivo or OPPO up to 100 W (only after disabling every protocol except 4.5V/21V in Custom Mode in the Anker Power app)
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, GaNPrime) FAQ

findings.label: Dell laptops
findings.value: Can show a 'Slow Charger' warning; Anker says to adjust the split in Custom Mode
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, GaNPrime) FAQ

findings.label: App account and iPhone 17 support
findings.value: Every feature works without logging in (guest account). iPhone 17 dynamic distribution needs the Anker app plus a firmware update
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) - Anker US
findings.note: The iPhone 17 firmware note is from the US product page. The no-login statement is FAQ Q1 at https://service.anker.com/eu/article-description/Anker-Prime-Charger-160W-3-Ports-GaNPrime-FAQ

findings.label: Price, Anker US
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) - Anker US
findings.note: Page also shows 'Save $34.00'. The 240W-cable bundle (anker.com/products/bundle-a2687-a88e2) was sold out.

findings.label: Per-port limits
findings.value: USB-C1 and USB-C2: 140 W (PD 3.1). USB-C3: 100 W (PD 3.0). USB-C4: 30 W (PD 3.0). USB-A: 22.5 W, no PD
findings.source_title: One charger for almost everything: 5-port Ugreen Nexode Pro 160W review - Notebookcheck Review
findings.note: Notebookcheck measured these with an FNB58 tester. In its box: the charger and a manual, with no cable listed. The Gadgeteer (2026-06-09, Rei Padla) gives C3 as 30 W and lists a 240W cable in the box, but that was a Chinese-plug launch unit, so I kept Notebookcheck's figures for the US unit.
